title: A weaker currency on AD/AS

predict.q: The economy starts below full employment. The currency depreciates by 10%. Other things equal, what happens?

options.s: AD shifts left, because more expensive imports reduce spending.
options.fb: More expensive imports cut import volumes and switch demand to home goods, so AD rises.

options.s: AD shifts right; real GDP and the price level both rise.
options.fb: Exports are cheaper abroad and imports dearer at home: net exports rise, AD shifts right along SRAS.

options.s: AS shifts right, because exports are now cheaper.
options.fb: Export prices affect demand (AD), not productive capacity (AS); if anything, higher input costs shift SRAS left.

options.s: The price level falls, because the country's goods are now cheaper.
options.fb: Cheaper exports raise demand, which pushes the price level up; more expensive imports also raise it.

task: Move the depreciation slider to 10% and watch AD, real GDP and the price level. Then switch on "dearer imported inputs" and watch SRAS.

target.do: Move the depreciation slider to 10%, then press Check.

takeaway: A depreciation raises net exports and AD; the price level rises.
